title: US Lowers Gas Mileage Rules for New Cars
summary:
How far can a car go on one gallon of gas? Right now, the US government has been pushing carmakers to make that number bigger every year. But on Monday, the Trump administration announced it is rolling those rules back.

Under the old Biden-era rules, new cars and trucks would have had to average more than 50 miles per gallon by 2031. The new rule sets the average at 34.9 miles per gallon. That means automakers have more freedom to build cars and trucks that use more gas.

The government says this will make new cars cheaper — about $1,300 less per vehicle. But David Shepardson, a reporter for Reuters, explained that drivers may end up paying more at the gas pump over the years. He said fuel costs over the life of a vehicle could rise by about $1,600 on average.

The change comes as the war in Iran has pushed oil prices up. It also makes it harder for electric cars to compete, because a $7,500 tax credit for buying an EV has ended. For now, no one knows exactly how the electric car market will change. A lot may depend on the next elections in 2028.
why_it_matters: Many families drive cars, so rules like these can change how much money they spend buying a car and filling it up with gas.

background_read: The United States has had rules about how much gas new cars may use since the 1970s, when a big oil shortage made gas prices jump.
President Donald Trump (the U.S. president since 2025) wants fewer of these rules; the rules being rolled back were made under Joe Biden (the president before him).
Gas mileage is measured in miles per gallon — the farther a car goes on one gallon, the less gas it needs.
